solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show behind schedule, finally interrupted by international church member

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word schedule only
something interrupted has another thing cutting into its middle, so a letter is pushed inside

blocks.note: to show one's behind is to moon, a crude prank
I is the standard abbreviation for international
the last letter of schedule

explanation.surface: A television show runs late and a missionary from a worldwide church barges in.
explanation.walkthrough: MOON plus E is broken into by I to give MOONIE. 'Show behind' reads as a programme overrunning, but it is the slang verb for baring one's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonies are followers of Sun Myung Moon's Unification Church, a popular nickname for its adherents.

clue.text: Sexual energy relinquished when going topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter

blocks.note: forgone means given up or done without

explanation.surface: Someone loses their libido the moment they strip off at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: FORGONE loses its first letter F to leave ORGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Reich coined the term for a supposed universal life force he linked to sexual drive and orgasm.

clue.text: European situation, read so cryptically, could have got Blair far

indicators.note: could have got signals that one set of letters, rearranged, would yield another

blocks.note: read as a crossword instruction, the first word means shake about, the anagram signal for what follows
these eleven letters, mixed up, spell the last two words of the answer

explanation.surface: A remark about how a European posting might have advanced a former Prime Minister's career.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read cryptically, ROCK OF GIBRALTAR says 'shake up OF GIBRALTAR', which gives GOT BLAIR FAR. Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rock is the limestone promontory at the southern tip of Spain, a British territory and so a place in Europe.

clue.text: Anxious new US check briefly involving a transnational currency

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the check word is dropped
involving means enclosing, so the outer pieces wrap round the currency

blocks.note: N is the usual abbreviation for new
the currency shared by many European nations
in America a check mark is what Britons call a tick

explanation.surface: Someone worries about a fresh American cheque drawn in euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a bank cheque in American spelling, but it is the mark placed against an item on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic person is excessively nervous and worried, so the adjective fits a fretful state.

clue.text: Shire ground crossed by kind old deer

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken down, so the letters are reworked
crossed by means having something placed across either side of it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: ilk means kind or sort
the word shire, mixed up

explanation.surface: An extinct deer wanders across a ploughed field in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: A shire is an English county, as in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish elk was a giant extinct deer of the Ice Age, hence a deer from long ago.

clue.text: Connection with trailer in which bachelor is introduced to drag queen

indicators.note: introduced to means brought into, so the degree goes inside the pair that follows

blocks.note: to drag something along is to tow it
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A cabaret where an unmarried man is presented to a drag artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' looks like one performer, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A towbar is the rigid fitting on the back of a car that couples it to a caravan or trailer.

clue.text: Almost insane to straddle minute old battlement

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for insane goes
to straddle is to sit with a leg on either side, so the letters go round

blocks.note: barking, as in barking mad, means crazy
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A nearly mad figure sits astride a tiny old castle wall.
explanation.walkthrough: BARKIN (BARKING less G) goes round M. Barking mad is British slang for completely crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmkin is an old Scottish and northern English term for a defensive wall or outer fortification.

clue.text: Open ballot box, causing upset

blocks.note: overt means done openly
a ballot box as a container, like an urn

explanation.surface: Opening the ballot box sparks an electoral shock.
explanation.walkthrough: An urn is a crossword stand-in for a ballot box, from the vessels once used to collect votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a result or object is to tip it over or reverse it completely, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One wearing a female's headgear

indicators.note: a thing wearing clothes has them wrapped round it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Tara is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up in a woman's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, so it counts as headwear.

clue.text: 50% of ordinary people taking minor routes in lake district?

indicators.note: half of a word is kept, here its opening half

blocks.note: the first half of normal, a synonym for ordinary
folk means people
B-roads are Britain's lesser roads, below A-roads

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk drive the back roads in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised Lake District of Cumbria is a red herring. NORMAL is halved to NOR. B-roads are secondary roads in the UK numbering system.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broads are a network of shallow lakes and rivers in eastern England, so a watery region with a question mark.

clue.text: Quarrel after drink – inferior stuff

indicators.note: after places the row word behind the drinking word in the across entry

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down
a beef is a grievance or quarrel

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after drinks, over something second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck is British slang for downing a drink quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck beef is the cheapest cut from a cow's neck, and figuratively anything coarse or of poor quality.

clue.text: North African Arab group historically dividing sheep

indicators.note: something dividing another splits it in two by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
the United Arab Republic, Egypt and Syria's union of 1958-61

explanation.surface: A history note about Arab tribes in North Africa splitting a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Historically' tells the solver the Arab group is a political union that no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuareg are Berber nomads of the Sahara, so a member is a North African person.

clue.text: Ironic language, at church, before my god

blocks.note: a tongue is a language
at a place is in it
CH is the abbreviation for church
an exclamation of alarm

explanation.surface: Someone blasphemes with an exclamation in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue-in-cheek remarks are said with mock seriousness, meant humorously rather than sincerely.

clue.text: Eats up Mr Silly's dishes

indicators.note: silly suggests foolishness, so the preceding letters are messed about

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A greedy Mr Men character polishes off his meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Silly is a character from the children's Mr Men books, whose name hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempuras are Japanese plates of battered, deep-fried seafood and vegetables, so they are servings of food.

clue.text: University upset about son causing bother

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the irritation word goes round the son

blocks.note: U for university
to nettle is to irritate
S for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A college is troubled over a student's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: U, then NETTLE wrapped round S. 'Upset' reads as an anagram signal but is a verb meaning irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or trouble them, a verb synonym for disquiet.

clue.text: Nuisance lowering head before one German artist

indicators.note: lowering the head moves the top letter down a place in this down entry

blocks.note: a pest is a nuisance
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A tiresome person bows before a German painter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the head is the top letter; lowering it swaps it with the letter beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a celebrated American-born British sculptor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: After return, yours truly and gaffer raise relief

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the first word runs backwards

blocks.note: yours truly is the writer, me
a gaffer is a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: After coming back, the writer and the manager build up some sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer is British slang for a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to carve or mould a design so it stands out from the surface, raising it in relief.

clue.text: Chemical compound stored in box, I'd expect

indicators.note: stored in means kept inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A chemist expects a compound to be kept in a sealed box.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a compound of oxygen with another element, such as rust.

clue.text: Again insist upon lock being put back on unfinished tower

indicators.note: put back means returned the way it came, so the hair word reads backwards
unfinished means lacking its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: to rear up is to tower
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a hair be replaced on top of a half-built tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like a noun but is a verb, to rise high.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert a claim is to state it forcefully once more, insisting upon it a second time.

clue.text: Sharp police unit infiltrating withdrawn US agents

indicators.note: infiltrating means slipping inside, so the police unit goes into the agency
withdrawn means pulled back, so the agency letters run backwards

blocks.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective branch

explanation.surface: Smart detectives penetrate a retreating American spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic tastes or remarks are tart and biting, so they are sharp in flavour or tone.

clue.text: Report concerning revolution

blocks.note: re means about
a turn is a revolution

explanation.surface: A briefing about a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is a formal statement or official account, as in a tax return or election return.

clue.text: Thick single bloke on report following loveless marriage

indicators.note: loveless means with no love, and love is the zero letter in tennis
following places the rest after the first piece in the across entry
on means placed after, so the single bloke pair comes second behind the report word

blocks.note: a marriage is a union
to report is to tell
the Roman numeral one
short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A single man gossips after a divorce with no love lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, so a loveless word drops its letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for stupid or slow-witted, a colloquial synonym for dim.

clue.text: Animal having to be sick around shrub

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the illness word runs backwards

blocks.note: a desert beast
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A beast feels unwell after eating round a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Camellias are evergreen flowering bushes from East Asia, a particular kind of garden plant.

clue.text: I called back old fool yesterday

indicators.note: back means the phone verb reads backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
rang, as on the telephone
O for old

explanation.surface: Someone phoned an old idiot the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then RANG reversed, then O. 'Yesterday' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignaro is an obsolete word for an ignorant person, a dunce from earlier times.
